name: KY-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 partisan lean in a Kentucky open seat
Massie lost renomination, but the GOP nominee inherits the seat
Democratic candidate raised under $100k with no outside spending
Prediction markets price the Democrat at about 3%
model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean and the collapse of Democratic fundraising to under $100,000 make an upset implausible; markets price the Republican near 96%. The open-seat dynamic after Massie's renomination loss shifts the margin modestly toward the Democrat, but not enough to change the category.
model.watch: A serious late Democratic outside-spending surge or a scandal involving the Republican nominee could tighten the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Thomas Massie (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Kentucky's 4th District is a heavily Republican open seat after Thomas Massie lost renomination. Ed Gallrein won the GOP nomination and enters the general with a large financial edge, having raised over $3.5 million and benefited from millions in outside spending on his behalf. Melissa Strange, the Democratic nominee, has raised under $100,000 and drawn no outside support.

The district's R+18 partisan lean makes a Democratic win very unlikely, and prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 96%. The forecast calls the race Safe Republican, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
